ahimsa.title: Ahimsa
ahimsa.one_line: Not causing injury to anyone, in any form, at any time, for any reason.
points: Ahimsa means not causing injury to anyone, including animals, in any form, at any time, or for any reason, in word, thought, or deed.
Guruji writes that if an injury has Vedic sanction, it does not constitute ahimsa.
Two animals hostile to each other will forget their hostility in the vicinity of those who practice absolute ahimsa.

sutra.translation: Upon being established in non-hurtfulness, there is a relinquishing of hostility in the presence of that (ahimsa).

aparigraha.title: Aparigraha
aparigraha.one_line: Non-possessiveness: taking only what is needed to sustain the body, and no more.
points: Aparigraha concerns the sustaining of the body: food and similar necessities should be pure (sattvic), untainted (nirmala), and acquired through righteousness, not through cheating, deceit, or persecution.
Guruji writes that taking only as much food as is needed to maintain the body, without desiring superfluous things of enjoyment, is aparigraha.
If aparigraha is firmly practiced, details of previous and future births are revealed to the yogi.

sutra.translation: Upon a foundation of non-possessiveness, there arises the full understanding of the wherefore of birth.

ardha-baddha-padma-paschimattanasana.title: Ardha Baddha Padma Paschimattanasana

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in the first Surya Namaskara.

Sit as in the 7th vinyasa of Paschimattanasana, stretch the left leg out, place the right leg on the left thigh, pressing the right heel into the navel, bring the right arm behind the back and grasp the big toe of the right foot, take the left foot with the left hand, and straighten the head and chest, doing puraka slowly.
Slowly place the chin on the outstretched left leg, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Slowly lift only the head.
Unfolding the legs and crossing them, as in Paschimattanasana, lift up the entire body with the strength of the arms.
Vinyasas 11–13 resemble the 4th, 5th, and 6th vinyasas of Paschimattanasana.

Back at the 7th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara, jump the legs through the arms on the strength of the hands alone, stretch the right leg out, place the left leg on the right thigh, grasp the left big toe with the left hand from behind, take the right foot with the right hand, straighten the head and chest.
Place the chin on the right knee, which is stretched out flat, and do puraka and rechaka slowly, as much as possible.
Lift the head only.
Unfold and cross the legs, lift the entire body up with the hands, and stay in this position.
Vinyasas 18–22 follow Paschimattanasana.

benefits: The practice of this asana alleviates the enlargement of the liver and spleen.
It also cures abdominal distention due to bad food and activities; the spoiling of the tissues due to a continually provoked vata; and weakness due to an inability to take food.
Constipation is also cured, and the operation of the bowels is rendered easy.

ardha-baddha-padmottanasana.title: Ardha Baddha Padmottanasana
notes: A sadhaka, or spiritual aspirant, should practice it under the careful guidance of a Guru.
Asanas such as this one, which involve both legs, are to be performed with the left leg as with the right.

sequence.action: Stand erect.

Place the right foot on the left thigh, pressing the heel into the lower abdomen, circle the right arm around the back, grasp the right big toe with the right hand, and place the left hand on the waist.
Slowly bend at the waist, press the left hand to the floor by the side of the left foot, straighten the knee, and touch the knee with the nose, doing puraka and rechaka slowly, as much as possible.
Lift the head only.
Stand up straight again, place left hand on waist.
Release the right leg, which is in the Padmasana form, and straighten it.

Place the left foot on the right thigh, bring the left arm around the back, take hold of the big toe of the left leg with the left hand, as outlined for the right, place right hand on waist, and stand.
As for the 2nd vinyasa, bend forward, place the right hand on the floor by the right leg, which is straight, and touch the knee with the nose, doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lift the head only.
Place the right hand on the waist and stand up straight.

benefits: The rectum, esophagus, and liver are purified by this asana.
It also prevents gas from occurring in the stomach, prevents diarrhea, and quells the gas that arises from inappropriate food. Should gas occur, it wards it off.
cautions: Ardha Baddha Padmottanasana can be practiced by anyone, including women of all ages, except those whose pregnancies have crossed into the fourth month.

If they concentrate their minds on their breathing only, the state of an asana will be spoiled. If, on the other hand, they concentrate only on an asana’s state, their rechaka and puraka will be spoiled. Therefore, it must again be stressed emphatically that these asanas be learned under the guidance of an able Guru.

asana.title: Asana
asana.one_line: The first of the six limbs of yoga per the Shandilya Upanishad and the first limb of hatha yoga per Swatmarama, practiced to bring the body and sense organs under control so disease cannot obstruct the deeper limbs.
points: Guruji writes that the Upanishads agree asana is the first step in the practice of the limbs of yoga, and quotes the Shandilya Upanishad naming six limbs: asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi — yama and niyama being included under the limbs of pratyahara and dharana.
Since Swatmarama and the Upanishadic sages agree on this six-limb view, Guruji states it is also acceptable to him.
Asana must be studied and practiced first because it is not possible to practice the limbs and sub-limbs of yama and niyama when the body and sense organs are weak and haunted by obstacles.
If asana is practiced according to established rules, diseases related to the body and sense organs can be prevented.
Guruji explains the word hatha: ha means the surya nadi and tha means the chandra nadi, and hatha yoga is the process of controlling the prana that moves through these two nadis.

Guruji states that hatha yoga and raja yoga are not different — if the mind moves toward the Self by means of hatha yoga, this is known as raja yoga, though many wrongly believe the two to be distinct.
There is no age limit for the practice of yoga; per Guruji it can be practiced by anyone eight years or older, regardless of sex, including the weak, the sick, and the disabled.
Pregnant women who have crossed into the fourth month should abstain from doing asanas.

For older people beginning yoga, Guruji lists ten sufficient asanas: Surya Namaskara (types 1 and 2), Paschimattanasana, Sarvangasana, Halasana, Karnapidasana, Urdhva Padmasana, Pindasana, Matsyasana, Uttana Padasana, and Shirshasana.
For the middle-aged, Guruji says it is best to do all the asanas, since the more they are practiced the stronger the body becomes and obstacles such as disease cease to be a problem.
As the bodily constitution of each person differs, the asanas must be practiced accordingly, and a Guru understands which asanas suit which practitioner.

Asana and Surya Namaskara must be practiced in accordance with the vinyasa method; without it, no part of the body becomes strong, the subtle nadis are not purified, and the body, sense organs, mind, and intellect fail to develop and may become further imbalanced.

sutra.sanskrit: Asanam pranasamrodhah pratyaharascha dharanam / Dhyanam samadhiretani shadangani prakirtita.
sutra.translation: Asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi are known as the six limbs.

quotes: It is said that asana is primary, due to its being the first limb of hatha yoga. One should practice that asana which is a state of steadiness, freedom from sickness, and lightness of body.

ashtanga.title: Ashtanga Yoga
ashtanga.one_line: The eight-limbed path that teaches how to make the mind one-pointed so as to see the Universal Self.
points: The word ashtanga means eight limbs, or steps.
The eight limbs are: yama; niyama; asana; pranayama; pratyahara; dharana; dhyana; and samadhi.
Ashtanga yoga is presented as the answer to the question of how the mind can be made one-pointed so that the Universal Self may be seen.

asteya.title: Asteya
asteya.one_line: Not stealing the property or possessions of others.
points: Asteya means not stealing the property or possessions of others.
Guruji writes that being envious of or begrudging another, cheating someone with sweet words, and gaining selfish ends under the guise of truthfulness are all to be abandoned.
Heaps of gems fall before the yogi who practices asteya, and he becomes the abode of all gems.

sutra.translation: Upon being established in non-stealing, there occurs the attainment of all prosperity.

baddha-konasana.title: Baddha Konasana
notes: Vamana speaks of Baddha Konasana as the greatest of the asanas.

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in earlier asanas, then the 7th vinyasa of Paschimattanasana.

Join the feet, fold them open, press the heels to the sivani nadi (the nadi between the anus and the genitals), hold the feet open with both hands, lift the chest, and sit with the knees on the floor.
Fold forward, place the head on the floor, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Remaining vinyasas as in earlier asanas.

while_holding: Do rechaka and tighten the anus fully.
Pull the stomach in completely, holding the lower abdomen and anus tightly, practicing rechaka and puraka.
benefits: By pulling the stomach in completely, holding the lower abdomen and anus tightly, and practicing rechaka and puraka, terrible afflictions related to the anus, such as constipation and piles, will be destroyed, and indigestion will no longer haunt an aspirant.
Many have had the experience of being relieved of bhagandara [fistula] and mulavyadhi [hemorrhoids] by this asana.
Thus, through its practice, diseases related to the anus and the dhatu will definitely be cured.

verses.sanskrit: Baddhakonasane tishtan gudamakunchayet buddha gudarognivrittih syat satyam satyam bravimyaham
verses.translation: The wise one should retract the anus while in Baddha Konasana as it wards off anal disease, this I declare is true.

cautions: But if an aspirant thinks that this will occur by his merely practicing asanas while continuing to eat rajasic [stimulating] and tamasic [heavy] foods, then he is misguided. Such a course will actually lead to an increase in sickness.
However, one should not abandon the practice of yoga after becoming disappointed or indifferent because of an inability to follow the sattvic diet strictly.

baddha-padmasana.title: Baddha Padmasana
notes: To be practiced after Shirshasana.
Yoga Mudra occurs in Baddha Padmasana, and is therapeutic for diseases.

sequence.action: Do the first six vinyasas of the first Surya Namaskara.
Sit and stretch the legs out, as in Paschimattanasana, and straighten the back and chest. Do rechaka and puraka.

Place the right foot on the left thigh and the left foot on the right thigh, press the heels of both feet into the lower abdomen on either side of the navel, reach around the back, take hold of the left big toe with the left hand and the right big toe with the right hand, push the chest forward, straighten the spinal column and waist, and bend the neck forward so that the chin presses into the chest. Do rechaka and puraka deeply.
Slowly place the chin on the floor, pull the navel in completely, and stiffen and push the body all the way forward. This is Yoga Mudra.
Stay, doing puraka and rechaka.
Without letting go of the toes, lift the head up, sit up straight, and push the chest out.
The next vinyasas follow those of preceding asanas.

while_holding: During Yoga Mudra, meditate upon one's chosen deity (ishta devata) while directing the gaze between the eyebrows, doing rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
benefits: Through Baddha Padmasana’s practice, the liver and spleen are purified, the spinal column straightened, and the anal canal remedied.
Thus, easy to do and very useful, its practice is desirable for everyone, from young to old.
quotes: The greatness of Baddha Padmasana has been affirmed by the Upanishads.
baddha-padmasana.benefits_source: Given in the book under Padmasana.

bhujapidasana.title: Bhujapidasana

sequence.action: Begin with the first six vinyasas of the first Surya Namaskara.

Using the strength of the arms, jump the legs around the shoulders without touching the floor, place one foot over the other, squeeze the shoulders forcefully with the thighs, and straighten the arms.
Without touching the legs or feet to the floor, touch only the chin to the floor, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Come back into the 7th vinyasa position.
Take back both legs without touching the floor, and balance them on the backs of the arms.
Come into the 4th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara.
The next vinyasas follow those specified earlier.

benefits: Bhujapidasana purifies the anna nala [food channel/esophagus], and the body becomes light, and the shoulders and waist become strong.

brahmacharya.title: Brahmacharya
brahmacharya.one_line: Establishing the mind in the supreme Brahman without allowing it to wander — not merely the retention of vital fluid or unmarried student life.
points: Guruji asks whether brahmacharya is merely the retention of vital fluid or unmarried student life, and answers that becoming one with the supreme Brahman alone is brahmacharya.

Our Shrutis and Smritis speak of eight types of obstacles to brahmacharya, given in a verse Guruji quotes: remembering, celebrating, amorous play, viewing, infatuated discussion, planning, determination, and the effort of one who has no partner — 'the wise declare these to be the eight limbs of romantic activity.'

Guruji writes that maintaining brahmacharya today is difficult because of theaters, pleasure houses, restaurants, and similar attractions, but that a man can still achieve some degree of it by avoiding vulgar company, crowded recreation, vulgar books, theaters and restaurants, and secret conversation with strangers of the opposite sex.
Guruji quotes the Bhagavad Gita (xvi:24): the sacred teaching (shastra) is one's measure of what is to be done and not done, and one should act according to what the shastra says.

Guruji writes that a householder does not lose brahmacharya through seminal loss by itself; in the truest sense, the householder alone can attain brahmacharya, citing a mantra that those who engage in romantic activity daily dissipate their energy, while those who delight when desire is in decline engage in true brahmacharya.

Guruji states plainly that if a man has intercourse with his wife during the daytime, his vitality is lost and death will conquer him quickly; he calls the argument that intercourse with other women is therefore acceptable the reasoning of 'perverted rationalists,' and states that intercourse with other women is always forbidden and harmful to brahmacharya even in thought.

According to the shastrakaras Guruji cites, sexual intercourse only at night and in accordance with the menstrual cycle allows even householders to be regarded as brahmacharis. For yogis, the night is judged further by the breath: if at night it moves through the surya nadi (right nostril), that is regarded as daytime; only when it moves through the chandra nadi (left nostril) at night is intercourse permitted. Guruji asks righteous householders, whether yogis or not, to reckon day and night this way.

Guruji writes that the interval between the fourth and sixteenth day of a woman's menstrual cycle is the correct time for intercourse according to scriptural experts; beyond the sixteenth day, on new and full moon days, and on other specified days, intercourse is not related to brahmacharya, and union with one's lawful wife should be for the sake of begetting good progeny only.
Guruji describes the promise made upon entering the householder stage: to do nothing apart from one's lawful wife with respect to dharma, artha, and kama.

Veerya (vitality) is described as the transformation of the thirty-second drop of blood into dhatu (semen); preserving the strength of the mind and sense organs requires preserving dhatu, and if it is lost, the strength of the mind and sense organs is also lost.

Guruji concludes that whether working, sleeping, eating, playing, or enjoying intercourse with one's wife, one should think of the Supreme Self at all times; if the mind is thus given to constant thought of the Supreme Self, its strength increases, and this strength is brahmacharya.
In truth, Guruji writes, establishing the mind in the supreme Brahman, without allowing it to wander here and there, is brahmacharya.

sutra.translation: Upon being established in brahmacharya, there is the attainment of vital energy.

quotes: This is only the question of perverted rationalists.

dharana.title: Dharana
dharana.one_line: The fourth of the six limbs named in the Shandilya Upanishad; Guruji does not treat it separately in this chapter beyond naming it.
points: Dharana is named as the fourth of the six limbs of yoga in the Shandilya Upanishad verse Guruji quotes.
Guruji states that yama and niyama are included under the limbs of pratyahara and dharana, but does not elaborate further on dharana itself in this chapter.

sutra.sanskrit: Asanam pranasamrodhah pratyaharascha dharanam / Dhyanam samadhiretani shadangani prakirtita.
sutra.translation: Asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi are known as the six limbs.

dhyana.title: Dhyana
dhyana.one_line: The fifth of the six limbs named in the Shandilya Upanishad; Guruji does not treat it separately in this chapter beyond naming it.
points: Dhyana is named as the fifth of the six limbs of yoga in the Shandilya Upanishad verse Guruji quotes.

sutra.sanskrit: Asanam pranasamrodhah pratyaharascha dharanam / Dhyanam samadhiretani shadangani prakirtita.
sutra.translation: Asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi are known as the six limbs.

garbha-pindasana.title: Garbha Pindasana

sequence.action: Do the six vinyasas described in earlier asanas, then sit as in the 7th vinyasa of Paschimattanasana.

Do Padmasana by placing the right foot on the left thigh and the left foot on the right thigh, insert both arms past the elbow through the openings between the thigh and calf, hold the ears with the hands, sitting purely on the buttocks, straighten the chest and spinal column, press both heels on either side of the navel, and remain in this position, doing rechaka and puraka as long as possible.

Bend the head forward completely, take hold of the head with the hands, and roll in a clockwise direction, doing rechaka on the roll back and puraka on the roll forward, until a full circle has been completed.
Roll forward and up, pressing the hands to the floor and lifting the body up off the floor.
The vinyasas and breathing that follow are described in foregoing asanas.

benefits: Garbha Pindasana dissolves the fat of the lower abdomen, purifies the manipura, or third, chakra, and wards off diseases of the liver and spleen.

halasana.title: Halasana

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–7 as in Sarvangasana.
Join together and raise the legs, as in Sarvangasana.

Slowly lower the legs to the floor over the head, keeping them straight, place the feet on the floor, lock the fingers behind the back, arms tight and straight, press the chin into the chest without bending the legs, and do puraka and rechaka deeply, as much as possible.
Remaining vinyasas as in Sarvangasana.

while_holding: Both rechaka and puraka occur in the 8th vinyasa.
benefits: Halasana purifies the intestines, the region of the waist, and the throat channel, and strengthens them.

By means of these five asanas, the vishuddhi chakra [throat chakra], heart, lungs, limbs, digestive system, and jathara [stomach] are purified, and perversions of the vital wind, which result in hiccups, dry cough, constipation, and indigestion, as well as high blood pressure, are warded off.
They also prevent illnesses such as asthma, and ailments related to the heart.
halasana.benefits_source: Given in the book under Pindasana, as the benefits of asanas 32 to 36; the last two apply to all five.

ishwarapranidhana.title: Ishwarapranidhana
ishwarapranidhana.one_line: Surrender to God: carrying out all actions without desiring their fruit, offering the fruit to the Lord.
points: Ishwarapranidhana means carrying out all our actions, spoken or unspoken, without desiring their fruit, and offering their fruit to the Lord.
Guruji quotes the great sages: whatever I do, whether out of desire or not, good or bad, having surrendered all that to you, I act as directed by you.
Through ishwarapranidhana, samadhi (union with the Supreme) is attained, which in turn leads to the attainment of perfection and fulfillment.

sutra.translation: The perfection of samadhi is due to the perfect alignment of attention with the omniscient seer within.

janu-shirshasana-a.title: Janu Shirshasana A

sequence.action: Sit as in Paschimattanasana, stretch the left leg out, press the area between the anus and the organ of generation with the heel of the right foot, pulling the right knee back 90 degrees, bend forward at the waist, take hold of the foot of the outstretched leg with both hands, tighten the anus and lower abdomen, straighten the back, and lift the head fully.
Place the forehead or chin on the knee of the outstretched leg, and do rechaka and puraka fully as much as possible.
Lift up the head slowly.
The next vinyasas follow those of preceding asanas.
Practice the same method for the other side; this is the 15th vinyasa and the state for that side.

while_holding: Do rechaka and puraka as deeply as possible while in the state of the asana.
benefits: Janu Shirshasana cures maladies such as muthra krcchra [burning while urinating], dhatu krcchra [semen loss], and diabetes.
Janu Shirshasana destroys these terrible afflictions, and purifies and strengthens the nadi known as sivani, which is related to the dhatu.
Janu Shirshasana (A & B) press on the virya nala for men, and Janu Shirshasana (C) presses on it for women, though all three are necessary and useful for both men and women alike.
In this way, diseases of the type just described will be cured, the fire of hunger increased, and food digested easily.
quotes: Janu Shirshasana, which some call Mahamudra, is of three types, each of which has twenty-two vinyasas.
janu-shirshasana-a.benefits_source: Given in the book under Janu Shirshasana (C), for all three types.
cautions: For all the asanas, the details of their breathing and vinyasa methods, as well as of how to remain in their states in accordance with the vinyasa method, have to be learned from a Guru.

janu-shirshasana-b.title: Janu Shirshasana B

sequence.action: Sit as in Paschimattanasana, stretch the left leg out straight, bend the right knee back 85 degrees, sit the anus directly on top of the right heel, take hold of the left foot with both hands, tighten the anus and lower abdomen, straighten the back, and lift the head fully.
Place the forehead or chin on the knee of the outstretched leg, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Slowly lift the head.
The next vinyasas follow those of preceding asanas.
Practice the same method for the other side; this is the 15th vinyasa and the state for that side.

benefits: Janu Shirshasana cures maladies such as muthra krcchra [burning while urinating], dhatu krcchra [semen loss], and diabetes.
Janu Shirshasana destroys these terrible afflictions, and purifies and strengthens the nadi known as sivani, which is related to the dhatu.
Janu Shirshasana (A & B) press on the virya nala for men, and Janu Shirshasana (C) presses on it for women, though all three are necessary and useful for both men and women alike.
In this way, diseases of the type just described will be cured, the fire of hunger increased, and food digested easily.
janu-shirshasana-b.benefits_source: Given in the book under Janu Shirshasana (C), for all three types.

janu-shirshasana-c.title: Janu Shirshasana C
notes: Janu Shirshasana can be practiced by anyone, man or woman, irrespective of age or sex.

sequence.action: Sit as in Paschimattanasana, stretch the left leg out straight, bring the right foot in toward the groin, twisting it so that the toes are pressed to the floor and the heel is pointing up toward the navel, press the right knee forward to a 45 degree angle, take hold of the left foot with both hands, straighten the back and arms, and tighten the anus and lower abdomen.
Folding at the waist, place the forehead or chin on the outstretched leg, press the right heel into the navel, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lift the head and straighten the arms.
The vinyasas that follow are as those in earlier asanas.
Practice the same method for the other side; this is the 15th vinyasa and the state for that side.

benefits: Janu Shirshasana cures maladies such as muthra krcchra [burning while urinating], dhatu krcchra [semen loss], and diabetes.
Janu Shirshasana destroys these terrible afflictions, and purifies and strengthens the nadi known as sivani, which is related to the dhatu.
Janu Shirshasana (A & B) press on the virya nala for men, and Janu Shirshasana (C) presses on it for women, though all three are necessary and useful for both men and women alike.
In this way, diseases of the type just described will be cured, the fire of hunger increased, and food digested easily.
quotes: By practicing Janu Shirshasana, the dhatu strengthens and, gradually, the vasana of kama [the tendency to desire] is destroyed.
janu-shirshasana-c.benefits_source: Given for all three types of Janu Shirshasana.

karnapidasana.title: Karnapidasana

sequence.action: Lie down, as in Sarvangasana.
Proceed to the 8th vinyasa of Sarvangasana.

Lower the legs to the floor, as in Halasana, bring the knees to the floor, take hold of the ears tightly with the knees, lower the arms to the floor, lock the fingers, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.

while_holding: Draw the stomach in fully without tightening the anus, and do rechaka and puraka.
benefits: Karnapidasana eliminates diseases of the ears, such as those that cause pus and blood to flow frequently, or a ringing in the ears.
It is thus better to cure them as early as possible with Karnapidasana.

By means of these five asanas, the vishuddhi chakra [throat chakra], heart, lungs, limbs, digestive system, and jathara [stomach] are purified, and perversions of the vital wind, which result in hiccups, dry cough, constipation, and indigestion, as well as high blood pressure, are warded off.
They also prevent illnesses such as asthma, and ailments related to the heart.
karnapidasana.benefits_source: Given in the book under Pindasana, as the benefits of asanas 32 to 36; the last two apply to all five.

kukkutasana.title: Kukkutasana

sequence.action: Do Garbha Pindasana through the 7th vinyasa: Padmasana, with the arms inserted through the space behind the knees.
Press the palms to the floor and lift up the Padmasana, standing on the strength of the palms. In this position, revolve the stomach (nauli), lift the back and chest fully, and do rechaka and puraka.
Come down slowly.
Remaining vinyasas as in Garbha Pindasana.

while_holding: Do rechaka and puraka deeply while keeping the chest, waist, and back completely straight.
With the heels pressing on either side of the navel and keeping the head lifted, do uddiyana bandha and nauli.
There is no mula bandha in this asana.
benefits: By means of Kukkutasana, the intestines are purified, the fat of the lower abdomen dissolved, and diseases affecting the bowels and urinary tract, as well as excess phlegm, are cured.

kurmasana.title: Kurmasana
notes: The state of the 9th vinyasa is called Supta Kurmasana (Reclined Tortoise).

sequence.action: Begin with the first six vinyasas of the first Surya Namaskara, as specified in earlier asanas.

Jump as in Bhujapidasana, lower down to the floor with the strength of the arms, stretch the arms out under the thighs, straighten the legs, put the chin on the floor, and lift the head to some extent.
Stay, doing rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
Bring the hands up behind the back and take hold of the wrist.
Cross the legs over each other, put the head on the floor, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible. This is Supta Kurmasana.
The next vinyasas follow those of Bhujapidasana.

benefits: Kurmasana purifies the kanda, or nerve plexus in the anal region from which all 72,000 nadis grow.
It also purifies the heart and lungs, and eliminates ailments caused by an imbalance of kapha dosha [phlegm].
The chest becomes broad, bad fat is dissolved, and the spinal column becomes strong.
Chest pain due to over-tiredness is cured, disorders from bad food remedied, and the fat in the lower abdomen dissolved, allowing the body to become healthy.

marichyasana-a.title: Marichyasana A
notes: Marichyasana was discovered by the sage Maricha, who gave it its name.
There are eight types of Marichyasana; the first four, described here, are related to yoga chikitsa (yoga therapy).

sequence.action: Stretch the left leg out as for the 7th vinyasa of Paschimattanasana, bend the right knee up, pull the right heel in toward the right buttock, take the right arm around the knee of the bent leg, bring the left hand behind the back and take hold of the right wrist, stretch the left leg, and raise the chest.
Place the forehead or chin on the knee of the outstretched leg, keeping the outstretched leg straight and tight, doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lift the head up.
Uth Pluthi.
Practice the same method for the left side; this is the 15th vinyasa and the state for that side.

benefits: The benefits of the four Marichyasanas are different, though all cure diseases in accordance with man’s physical nature.
They each cure gaseous movements in the stomach and intestines, as well as movements of the rectum, such as diarrhea, and restore digestive power.
With that, flatulence, indigestion, and constipation are eliminated.
Some women suffer from abdominal pain during menstruation. This is removed by the practice of these asanas.
The womb becomes powerful and enables a woman to carry a child strongly, and miscarriage due to weakness is cured.
The vata pitta kosha [large intestine and gall bladder] are purified, as is the manipura chakra [the third chakra at the navel center], and the body gains strength and power.
marichyasana-a.benefits_source: Given in the book under Marichyasana (D), for all four.

There should be no error in sitting firmly and holding the hands and legs.
Pregnant women should not practice this asana after the second month.

marichyasana-b.title: Marichyasana B

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in the first Surya Namaskara.

Sit with the legs stretched out, bring the left heel toward the navel as in Padmasana, bend the right knee, sit firmly with the right knee bent and right heel pulled toward the right buttock, bring the right arm around the right shin, and grasp hold of the left wrist with the right hand.
Touch the nose to the floor, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lift the head and straighten the chest.
Follow the method of vinyasa specified in earlier asanas.
The same for the left side; this is the 15th vinyasa and the state for that side.

They each cure gaseous movements in the stomach and intestines, as well as movements of the rectum, such as diarrhea, and restore digestive power.

marichyasana-c.title: Marichyasana C

sequence.action: Sit in the same manner as above, stretch the left leg out, press the right foot to the right buttock as in Marichyasana (A), straighten the chest, turn the waist toward the right, bring the left arm around the front of the right knee, twisting the left hand and arm around toward the back, bring the right arm around the back and grasp the left wrist with the right hand, straighten and turn the chest and waist fully, doing rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
The vinyasas that follow are specified in earlier asanas.
The same for the left side; this is the 12th vinyasa and the state for that side.

benefits: The benefits of the four Marichyasanas are different, though all cure diseases in accordance with man’s physical nature.
They each cure gaseous movements in the stomach and intestines, as well as movements of the rectum, such as diarrhea, and restore digestive power.

marichyasana-d.title: Marichyasana D

sequence.action: Sit, bending the arms and legs as in Marichyasana (B), turn the waist, bring the left arm around the front of the right knee and around toward the back as in Marichyasana (C), bring the right arm around the back and take hold of the left wrist with the right hand, turn the waist fully, lift the chest, doing rechaka and puraka slowly and deeply, as much as possible.
The same for the left side; this is the 12th vinyasa and the state for that side.
The method for the vinyasas has been specified earlier.

benefits: The benefits of the four Marichyasanas are different, though all cure diseases in accordance with man’s physical nature.
They each cure gaseous movements in the stomach and intestines, as well as movements of the rectum, such as diarrhea, and restore digestive power.
With that, flatulence, indigestion, and constipation are eliminated.
Some women suffer from abdominal pain during menstruation. This is removed by the practice of these asanas.
The womb becomes powerful and enables a woman to carry a child strongly, and miscarriage due to weakness is cured.
The vata pitta kosha [large intestine and gall bladder] are purified, as is the manipura chakra [the third chakra at the navel center], and the body gains strength and power.

There should be no error in sitting firmly and holding the hands and legs.
Pregnant women should not practice this asana after the second month.

matsyasana.title: Matsyasana

sequence.action: Lie down, as in Sarvangasana.
Doing puraka, in Padmasana, press the hands to the floor on either side of the head.

Doing rechaka, lift the head up and place the crown of the head on the floor, bend the back up by lifting the waist, take hold of the feet, and straighten the arms. Stay, doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.

Doing puraka and next rechaka, lower the head, unfold the legs from Padmasana, hold the legs and feet as in Halasana, place the hands next to the ears, and roll over into the 4th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara. This is called Chakrasana.
The next vinyasas are the same as those in earlier asanas.

benefits: Matsyasana and Uttana Padasana counterpose the five asanas that precede them and remove the shoulder and waist pain that result from their practice.
They also purify the esophagus and anus, as well as the liver and spleen, and furnish the waist and neck with increasing strength.
matsyasana.benefits_source: Given in the book for Matsyasana and Uttana Padasana together.

navasana.title: Navasana

sequence.action: The first six vinyasas of this asana follow those of the first Surya Namaskara.

Jump the legs in between the arms using only the strength of the arms, without letting the body or legs touch the floor, sit squarely on the buttocks, raise and straighten the legs, sit in the form of a boat, straighten the chest, waist, and legs, and hold the arms out straight on either side of the knees.
Stay in the boat, doing rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
Cross the legs without touching the floor, and use the strength of the arms and hands to lift the body up off the floor.
Come back to the 7th vinyasa.
Repeat the asana three to six times.
The vinyasas that follow have been specified earlier.

while_holding: Never do kumbhaka (hold the breath) while coming into the state of this asana.
benefits: The anal channel, spinal column, ribs, and lower abdomen are purified by Navasana.
It also cures gastric trouble resulting from food not digesting completely and provoked vata due to a lack of digestive fire.
The waist additionally gains strength.

niyama.title: Niyama
niyama.one_line: The second limb of ashtanga yoga, consisting of five observances.
points: Niyama is the second of the eight limbs of ashtanga yoga.
It has five sub-limbs: shaucha; santosha; tapas; swadhyaya; and ishwarapranidhana.

padahastasana.title: Padahastasana

sequence.action: Stand with the legs half a foot apart, as in Padangushtasana.
Place the palms under the feet.
Lift the head up and stay in position.
Place the head in the region between the knees, keeping knees straight, and hold position, doing rechaka and puraka fully as much as possible.
Lift only the head.
Return to Samasthiti, as in the earlier asana.

while_holding: Draw the lower abdomen in tightly.
Rechaka and puraka done as much as possible.
benefits: Padahastasana purifies the anal canal, kidneys, and lower abdomen.

padangushtasana.title: Padangushtasana

sequence.action: Stand up straight, inhaling deeply through the nostrils.
Jump the legs half a foot apart, reach down and take hold of the big toes, lift head and chest fully, knees straight.
Stay in position.
Draw in the lower abdomen, head between the two knees, knees straight. Stay, doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Slowly lift the head, fingers still holding the big toes.
Return to Samasthiti.

while_holding: Draw the lower abdomen in and hold it tightly.
Rechaka and puraka slowly and as much as possible.
benefits: Padangushtasana dissolves the fat of the lower abdomen, and purifies both the kanda, or egg-shaped nerve plexus in the anal region, and the rectum.

padmasana.title: Padmasana
notes: Also called Kevala, or Simple, Padmasana.
Useful for the practice of pranayama, dhyana, sandhya vandana, and puja.
One should sit in Kevala Padmasana after doing Baddha Padmasana.

sequence.action: Follow the vinyasas above for Baddha Padmasana through the 7th vinyasa.

Place the right foot on the left thigh and the left foot on the right thigh, press the heels into the lower abdomen on either side of the navel, make the knees rest on the floor, place the hands on the knees, sit up, and straighten the back, chest, and waist. This is Padmasana. Stay, doing rechaka and puraka deeply and slowly as many times as possible.
The next vinyasas are as those in earlier asanas.

benefits: The sages and seers of works such as the Yoga Yagnavalkya and Yoga Vashishta have said that the practice of Padmasana destroys not only diseases of the body, but great sins, as well.
Therefore, as Padmasana is the best and greatest of the asanas, and easy to practice in all respects, it should be performed by everyone.

parshvottanasana.title: Parshvottanasana
notes: Rechaka and puraka are as in Trikonasana.
All the asanas described so far loosen the limbs of the body, which aids movement and renders the practice of subsequent asanas easier. They can be done by men and women of all ages.

sequence.action: Jump to the right, standing with the legs three feet apart, as described in Trikonasana, bring hands together behind the back in a prayer position, turn the right foot and waist to the right, and lift the chest.
Slowly touch the nose to the knee without bending the knees, and hold position, doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lift the head up and turn to face the left, following the method for the 1st vinyasa.
Touch the knee with the nose and hold, while doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lift the head and chest, using the strength of the waist, and stand up straight.
Return to Samasthiti.

benefits: Like Prasarita Padottanasana, Parshvottanasana eliminates the bad fat at the waist, which makes the lower abdomen thin, the waist strong, and the body light.
quotes: For people suffering from rheumatic or joint pain, the first and second Surya Namaskara and first six asanas are especially important. Done properly with rechaka and puraka, they eliminate the pain that occurs in the joints, and help the body to become light and healthy.
cautions: It is very important, however, that the particulars of the vinyasas above be kept in mind during practice by those who are weak or ill. As these are very difficult to convey to aspirants, however much the correct method for doing the asanas is described, it is better that they learn them from a Guru first, and then practice them.

paschimattanasana.title: Paschimattanasana
notes: There are three types of Paschimattanasana: (1) holding the big toes and touching the nose to the knees; (2) holding either side of the feet and touching the nose to the knees; (3) locking the hand and wrist beyond the feet and touching the chin to the knee. All three types should be practiced, as each is useful.

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in the first Surya Namaskara.

With only the strength of the arms, jump the legs between the hands without allowing them to touch the floor, and stretch out the legs. Press the hands to the floor on either side of the hips, straighten the chest and waist, lower the head a little, draw the anus up tightly, lift the lower abdomen and hold firmly, and sit erect, slowly doing rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
Grasp and hold the upper parts of the feet (as your practice becomes firm, you should be able to lock your hands behind your feet).
Slowly straighten both legs, and place the head between the knees.
Slowly lift only the head.
Let go of the feet, press the hands to the floor, bend the legs, and lift the entire body up off the floor merely with the strength of the arms.
Vinyasas 12–16 as in the Surya Namaskara.

while_holding: Puraka and rechaka slowly and deeply, as much as possible.
Retract and hold the anus tightly, squeeze the lower abdomen and hold it in, and concentrate on the nadis related to the kanda.
benefits: The practice of this asana helps the stomach to become slender by dissolving its fat.
It also increases jathara agni [the fire of hunger], helps food to digest well, and strengthens the organs of the digestive systems (jir-nanga kosha).

In addition, it cures weakness in the hands and legs resulting from a loss of appetite and low digestive fire, as well as indolence and giddiness stemming from an aberration in the liver, and gas problems in the stomach.
quotes: As there is no place for the apana vayu [downward-flowing prana, or energy], which circulates in the anus, to go, it moves upward and becomes one with prana vayu [upward-moving prana]. When this occurs, an aspirant has nothing to fear from old age and death

verses.sanskrit: Iti Paschimattanam asanagyam Pavanam paschimavahinam karoti / Udayam jatharanalasya kuryadudare karshyamarogatam cha pumsam.
verses.translation: Principle among asanas, Paschimattanasana causes vital energy to be carried up the spine. As well, it should lead to the rising of the digestive fire, slenderness in the abdomen, and freedom from sickness for all.

pindasana.title: Pindasana
notes: Sarvangasana and Shirshasana are together called viparita karani.
These seven asanas must be practiced in this order, which must never vary: Sarvangasana, Halasana, Karnapidasana, Urdhva Padmasana, Pindasana, Matsyasana, and Uttana Padasana.
After finishing these seven, one should never go on to an asana such as Paschimattanasana; only Matsyasana, Uttana Padasana, and Shirshasana should follow.

sequence.action: Follow the vinyasas of Urdhva Padmasana above through to the 9th vinyasa.

Doing puraka and then rechaka, bring the legs in Padmasana slowly down to the forehead, envelop the thighs with the arms, embrace the Padmasana, hold the wrists tightly, and balance the body on the shoulders only. Stay, slowly doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Subsequent vinyasas are as those of Sarvangasana.

benefits: Pindasana purifies the lower abdomen, the spinal column, liver and spleen, and the stomach.

By means of these five asanas, the vishuddhi chakra [throat chakra], heart, lungs, limbs, digestive system, and jathara [stomach] are purified, and perversions of the vital wind, which result in hiccups, dry cough, constipation, and indigestion, as well as high blood pressure, are warded off.
They also prevent illnesses such as asthma, and ailments related to the heart.
pindasana.benefits_source: The last two are given in the book for all five asanas from Sarvangasana to Pindasana.

verses.sanskrit: Maranam bindu patena jivanam bindu dharanat
verses.translation: The falling of the drop is death, while retaining bindu is life.
verses.source: A scriptural statement, as quoted by Guruji

pranayama.title: Pranayama
pranayama.one_line: The second of the six limbs, the practice of taking in the subtle power of the vital wind through rechaka, puraka, and kumbhaka in conjunction with the three bandhas, by which the mind is arrested and the diseases of body, sense organs, and mind are cured.
points: Guruji writes that there are many kinds of pranayama: Sri Shankara Bhagavadpada speaks of a thousand and explains their methods, while Swatmarama names but eight — suryabedana, ujjayi, sitkari, shitali, bhastrika, bhramari, murchha, and plavini. Of these, Guruji says only four are suitable for us.
Some pranayamas are useful for curing diseases, some for purification of the nadis, and some for the arrest of the mind, but all require that asana be practiced first.

Pranayama is not simply taking in the breath and letting it out through the nostrils; it means taking in the subtle power of the vital wind through rechaka (exhalation), puraka (inhalation), and kumbhaka (breath retention), practiced together with the three bandhas — mula bandha, uddiyana bandha, and jalandhara bandha.

Through pranayama the mind becomes arrested in a single direction and follows the movement of the breath, per the Hatha Yoga Pradipika verse that the breath in motion means the mind is moving, and the breath without motion means the mind must be motionless.

In hatha yoga there are thousands of methods of pranayama — some purify the nadis, some purify and strengthen the body, some cure diseases and purify the seven dhatus, and others lead to the cessation of the mind and knowledge of Brahman. Among these, Guruji says kumbhaka pranayama is the most important, quoting Shankara Bhagavadpada that among a thousandfold kumbhas, the pure kumbha alone is highly esteemed.

Guruji warns that pranayama must be learned under the direction of a Guru and never attempted by one who thinks a reading of the scriptures makes him an expert; he quotes the Hatha Yoga Pradipika's warning that prana, like a lion, elephant, or tiger, must be brought under control only gradually — otherwise it destroys the practitioner.
If practiced while violating the rules, or with pride and feigned expertise, the aspirant puts himself in danger.

Guruji lays out rules of food, sex, and speech for the practitioner: sattvic foods are best; sour, salty, or spicy foods and vegetables consumed in quantity are unpleasant for practitioners; only half the stomach should be taken up by food, one quarter by water, and one quarter left to the movement of air; too much talk destroys the power of the tongue and speech; too much sex weakens the body, sense organs, and mind.
The place of practice should be spotlessly clean and level, have windows, and be suitable for smearing with cow dung — never in the open air, an unclean or malodorous place, a basement, or a roof.

Sweat formed during practice should be rubbed back into the body by hand, not dried in the open air, which saps the body's strength over time; per the Hatha Yoga Pradipika, rubbing the body with the perspiration of exertion produces firmness and lightness of the body.
During the period of yoga practice it is advisable to take in much milk and ghee; for the first three months, cold-water bathing and fasting are to be avoided.

Guruji quotes the Hatha Yoga Pradipika that yoga is accomplished by six things — enthusiasm, boldness, firmness, discrimination of truth, conviction, and avoidance of public gatherings — and that whether young, old, very old, sick, or debilitated, one who is vigilant attains success in all the yogas by practice.

Pregnant women past the fourth month may practice ujjayi, samavritti, and vishamavritti pranayama without kumbhaka until the seventh month, seated in Padmasana or Mahamudra, for a smoother delivery. For the very old, who find certain asanas too difficult, Guruji recommends daily mahabandha along with rechaka kumbhaka, puraka kumbhaka, samavritti vishamavritti, and sithali pranayama.

sutra.sanskrit: Suryabhedanamujjayi sithkari shithali tatha / Bhastrika bhramari murccha plaviniti ashtakumbhakah.
sutra.translation: Suryabedana, ujjayi, sitkari, shitali, bhastrika, bhramari, murchha, and plavini are the eight kumbhakas.

quotes: Just as a lion, elephant or tiger may be gradually brought under control, so is prana attended to. Otherwise it destroys the practitioner.

prasarita-padottanasana-a.title: Prasarita Padottanasana A
notes: In the 2nd vinyasa, both rechaka and puraka are to be performed.

sequence.action: Jump to the right, spreading the legs as much as five feet apart, as in Utthita Parshvakonasana, and place the hands on the waist.
Press the hands to the floor with the fingertips in line with the big toes.
Keep the head lifted, breathing in slowly.

Place the head on the floor between the hands, keeping the legs straight and tight, and hold position with waist lifted, doing puraka and rechaka as much as possible. The stomach should be drawn in properly, using only the uddiyana bandha (stomach lock), and by slightly loosening the mula bandha (anal lock).
Lift and hold the head up completely.
Hold the head up.
Lift the hands and place them on the waist, and return to the position of the 1st vinyasa.
Return to Samasthiti.

benefits: If this is done, the anal canal will be purified, the bad fat in the lower abdomen will dissolve, the waist will become thin and strong, and the body will become light and beautiful.
This asana also cures constipation, and purifies the top part of the spinal column and the waist.
prasarita-padottanasana-a.benefits_source: Given in the book under Prasarita Padottanasana (D), for all four parts.
cautions: Great attention should be paid to the stomach and the anal channel while practicing the four parts of Prasarita Padottanasana.
It is best to learn the proper method from a Guru.

prasarita-padottanasana-b.title: Prasarita Padottanasana B
notes: This is the second part of Prasarita Padottanasana.
Aspirants should note that in each part of Prasarita Padottanasana, both rechaka and puraka occur in the same vinyasas.

sequence.action: Stand, as in Prasarita Padottanasana (A), stretch the arms out to the sides at chest level and straighten them, as in Trikonasana, and hold position.
Place the hands on the waist.
Place the head slowly on the floor, using the strength of the waist and legs, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Without placing the hands on the floor, lift the head up, using only the strength of the waist and legs, and stand up straight.
Bring the arms out wide at the level of the chest, as described in the 1st vinyasa, and hold position.

benefits: If this is done, the anal canal will be purified, the bad fat in the lower abdomen will dissolve, the waist will become thin and strong, and the body will become light and beautiful.
This asana also cures constipation, and purifies the top part of the spinal column and the waist.
prasarita-padottanasana-b.benefits_source: Given in the book under Prasarita Padottanasana (D), for all four parts.
cautions: Great attention should be paid to the stomach and the anal channel while practicing the four parts of Prasarita Padottanasana.
It is best to learn the proper method from a Guru.

prasarita-padottanasana-c.title: Prasarita Padottanasana C

sequence.action: Place the hands on waist and stand, as in (A) and (B) above.
Lock the fingers behind the back, swell the chest, and stand.
Slowly place the head on the floor, straightening and tightening both the arms and legs, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Without unlocking the hands, lift the head up, using the strength of the waist only.
Unlock the hands from behind the back and place them on the waist.
Return to Samasthiti.

benefits: If this is done, the anal canal will be purified, the bad fat in the lower abdomen will dissolve, the waist will become thin and strong, and the body will become light and beautiful.
This asana also cures constipation, and purifies the top part of the spinal column and the waist.
prasarita-padottanasana-c.benefits_source: Given in the book under Prasarita Padottanasana (D), for all four parts.
cautions: Great attention should be paid to the stomach and the anal channel while practicing the four parts of Prasarita Padottanasana.
It is best to learn the proper method from a Guru.

prasarita-padottanasana-d.title: Prasarita Padottanasana D

sequence.action: Stand with the legs apart, as in Prasarita Padottanasana (A), and place the hands on the waist.
Take hold of the big toes and lift the head, keeping the arms and spine straight.
Place the center of the head on the floor in line with the feet, keeping the legs straight and the lower abdomen pulled in, and breathe fully and deeply as much as possible.
Lift the head up completely.
Hold.
Lift the hands, place them on the waist, and return to the position of the 1st vinyasa.
Return to Samasthiti.

benefits: If this is done, the anal canal will be purified, the bad fat in the lower abdomen will dissolve, the waist will become thin and strong, and the body will become light and beautiful.
This asana also cures constipation, and purifies the top part of the spinal column and the waist.
prasarita-padottanasana-d.benefits_source: Given for all four parts of Prasarita Padottanasana.
cautions: Great attention should be paid to the stomach and the anal channel while practicing the four parts of Prasarita Padottanasana.
It is best to learn the proper method from a Guru.

pratyahara.title: Pratyahara
pratyahara.one_line: The third of the six limbs named in the Shandilya Upanishad; Guruji does not treat it separately in this chapter beyond naming it.
points: Pratyahara is named as the third of the six limbs of yoga in the Shandilya Upanishad verse Guruji quotes.
Guruji states that yama and niyama are included under the limbs of pratyahara and dharana, but does not elaborate further on pratyahara itself in this chapter.

sutra.sanskrit: Asanam pranasamrodhah pratyaharascha dharanam / Dhyanam samadhiretani shadangani prakirtita.
sutra.translation: Asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi are known as the six limbs.

purvatanasana.title: Purvatanasana
notes: Purvatanasana represents Paschimattanasana's opposite.
Immediately after an asana that bends the body forward, one that bends it backward is to be done, and a backward bend is to be followed immediately by a forward bend.

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–7 as in Paschimattanasana.

Place the hands on the floor at a distance of twelve inches behind the waist, lift the legs and torso entirely off the floor, press the soles of the feet firmly on the floor, lower the head back, making the body firm, and hold, while slowly performing rechaka and puraka.
Slowly return to the state of the 7th vinyasa and sit.
The remaining vinyasas that complete this asana follow those of Paschimattanasana.

benefits: Purvatanasana purifies and strengthens the heart, anus, spinal column, and waist.
quotes: From this, any pain in the waist resulting, for example, from Paschimattanasana, will disappear.

samadhi.title: Samadhi
samadhi.one_line: The sixth and final limb named in the Shandilya Upanishad; Guruji does not treat it separately in this chapter beyond naming it.
points: Samadhi is named as the sixth of the six limbs of yoga in the Shandilya Upanishad verse Guruji quotes.

sutra.sanskrit: Asanam pranasamrodhah pratyaharascha dharanam / Dhyanam samadhiretani shadangani prakirtita.
sutra.translation: Asana, pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi are known as the six limbs.

santosha.title: Santosha
santosha.one_line: Contentment: an even mind, unmoved by fortune or misfortune, honor or dishonor.
points: Guruji writes that ordinary happiness from a sudden rise in income or a windfall is momentary and short-lived.
Whether one is rich or poor, whether fortune smiles or not, whether honor or dishonor comes, one should never feel dejected.
Santosha is keeping the mind focused in a single direction, always being happy, and never feeling regret for any reason.
If santosha is practiced, unsurpassed joy comes.

sutra.translation: Owing to contentment, there is an unexcelled attainment of happiness.

sarvangasana.title: Sarvangasana
notes: The next five asanas are related to Sarvangasana; the book gives their benefits together after Pindasana, and they are shown on each asana here.

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in the first Surya Namaskara.
Coming into the 7th vinyasa of Paschimattanasana, lie down, arms by the sides and legs straight. Do puraka and rechaka four to five times, deeply.

With the legs held straight and tightly together, slowly raise the legs up over the head, and put the full weight of the body on the shoulders only, hands holding the waist, elbows pressed to the floor.
Lower the legs toward the head, place the hands on the floor on either side of the head, push the legs back and behind, and lifting the head, come into the 4th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara.
Remaining vinyasas as in earlier asanas.

while_holding: The chin should press into the chest properly, the legs held straight, and the big toes and the tip of the nose should form a single line.
Stay in this state for five, ten, fifteen, even thirty minutes, doing rechaka and puraka deeply.
benefits: Sarvangasana cures all diseases, purifies the vishuddhi chakra, and makes the amrita bindu firm.
Sarvangasana purifies the heart, lungs, and all other parts of the body by making the blood hot.

By means of an asana such as Sarvangasana, ailments of the throat or those likely to affect the throat, are destroyed, including the inability to pronounce words clearly, throat pain, and diseases associated with the heart.
Sarvangasana also purifies the base of the throat (kanta kupa), prevents choking, and stops the appearance of boils caused by internal heat.
In addition, musicians who practice this asana for a period of time will find that it helps their singing become melodious and tuneful.

By means of these five asanas, the vishuddhi chakra [throat chakra], heart, lungs, limbs, digestive system, and jathara [stomach] are purified, and perversions of the vital wind, which result in hiccups, dry cough, constipation, and indigestion, as well as high blood pressure, are warded off.
They also prevent illnesses such as asthma, and ailments related to the heart.
sarvangasana.benefits_source: Given in the book under Pindasana, as the benefits of asanas 32 to 36; the last two apply to all five.

satya.title: Satya
satya.one_line: Truthfulness in thought, word, and deed.
points: Satya is truthfulness; one should always tell the truth in thought, word, and deed.
Guruji writes that the truth must be pleasant to others, and that an unpleasant truth should not be uttered.
If one follows the truth in this manner, all one's words will become true and all one's desires will be fulfilled.

sutra.translation: Upon being established in truth, there is surety in the result of actions.

setu-bandhasana.title: Setu Bandhasana
notes: The asanas described so far are organized systematically and should only be practiced in the order in which they are presented. One asana must not be performed at the expense of another, because the muscles on one side of the body will become strong while those on the other will weaken.
When time is short, it is not necessary to practice every asana, though those that are done should be practiced in a systematic manner.

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in earlier asanas.
Lie down, as in Supta Padangushtasana.
Inhale.

Bend the knees a little, join the heels together, placing the little toes firmly on the floor, bend the head back, place the top of the head on the floor, lift the chest a little, and maintain position, bending the back.
Cross the arms over the chest, lift up the waist and back, and stand straightly on the head and feet alone, while doing rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
Slowly lie down.
Raise the straightened legs toward the head, and press the hands to the floor on either side of the head.
Lift the head and roll the body over on the strength of the arms, coming into the 4th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara.
Remaining vinyasas as in previous asanas.

benefits: Setu Bandhasana purifies and strengthens the waist and neck, purifies the muladhara chakra [root chakra], and increases the jathara agni, or digestive fire.
It also purifies the esophagus, heart, and lungs, making them strong.
cautions: They can be practiced by anyone, men and women alike, except by women who are more than four months pregnant.
This does not mean, however, that they should be learned from pictures or books. On the contrary, they should be practiced under the tutelage of a benevolent Satguru.

shaucha.title: Shaucha
shaucha.one_line: Purification, of two kinds: external washing of the body and internal purification of the mind through universal friendliness.
points: There are two types of shaucha: bahir shaucha (external purification) and antah shaucha (internal purification).
Bahir shaucha involves washing the outer body with red clay and water; rubbing the body with clay removes sweat and dirt and makes the body soft and shiny.
Antah shaucha means viewing everything and every being as a friend (maitri), treating all with affection, and considering everything a reflection of God.

Guruji writes that from this twofold shaucha, a loathing develops for the body, seen as abominable, essenceless, and perishable, and a disgust is felt when touching the body of another, leading one to hesitate to indulge in sin.

sutra.translation: Owing to purity, there is a desire to protect one's own body, being the non-contact with whatever is adverse (to that).

shirshasana.title: Shirshasana
notes: Also known as Kapalasana or Viparita Karani.

sequence.action: While coming from the 6th to the 7th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara, sit on the knees, lock the fingers together, and place the elbows on the floor.
Doing rechaka and then puraka, place the crown of the head on the floor, interlocked hands cupping the back of the head.

Doing rechaka and puraka again, straighten the legs and, keeping them together and straight, lift them up with the power of the arms, tighten the body, point the toes, and keep the body erect using the strength of the arms. Stay, doing rechaka and puraka slowly and as many times as possible.
Doing rechaka slowly, bring the feet back down onto the floor, rest with the buttocks on the heels and the head on the floor for two minutes.
Doing puraka and then rechaka, jump back into the 4th vinyasa of the first Surya Namaskara.
The next vinyasas are as those described above.

while_holding: Draw the lower abdomen and the anus in fully and hold them tightly — mula bandha.
Keep the entire body erect.
Do rechaka and puraka deeply, without kumbhaka.
Begin by staying five minutes, then ten, then fifteen, increasing the time in the state by five-minute increments over many days, months, and years, until able to stay for a full three hours.
benefits: Through the practice of Shirshasana, the subtle nadis of the head—that is, those related to the brain and sense organs, such as the eyes—are purified by an inflow of warm blood, and the power of memory is increased.
Eye disease is destroyed, the eyes glow, and long-sightedness improves.
The five sense organs, too, become purified.
cautions: Pregnant women should not practice this asana.
Aspirants should note that merely putting the head down and legs up, and then standing upside down is not Shirshasana; very simply, this is wrong.
For example, the entire body must stand upside down on the strength of the arms alone.
Hence, aspirants should never practice Shirshasana first.
Moreover, following Shirshasana, they should only sit in Padmasana and do pranayama and the like, but no further asanas.

verses.translation: We can dwell in (Shirshasana) for three hours.
verses.source: A scriptural saying, as quoted by Guruji

verses.sanskrit: Maranam bindu patena / Jivanam bindu dharanat / Tasmat sarvaprayatnena / Bindu dharanam abhyaset
verses.translation: Loss of bindu is death / and the preservation of it, life / So, by all means / is the holding of bindu to be preserved.
verses.source: The yoga shastra, as quoted by Guruji

verses.sanskrit: Yuva vrddho’tivrddho va vyadito durbalo’pi va / Abhyasat siddhim apnoti / Sarvayogeshvatandritah
verses.translation: Whether young or old, or very old / sick or debilitated / one who is vigilant attains, by means of practice, success in all the yogas.

supta-konasana.title: Supta Konasana

sequence.action: Vinyasas 1–6 as in the first Surya Namaskara.
As in Paschimattanasana, lie flat on the floor, legs together, and stretch the legs out tightly.
Exhale.
Lift both legs up, as in Sarvangasana.
Bring the legs over the head, holding them as in Halasana, place the full weight of the body on the shoulders, and hold the big toes with the hands, legs wide apart.
Do rechaka and puraka.
Without bending the legs, come up into the 9th vinyasa of Upavishta Konasana.
Slowly lower into the 8th vinyasa of Upavishta Konasana.
Lift only the head.
Remaining vinyasas as in earlier asanas.

while_holding: Draw the abdomen in completely, but without mula bandha or even uddiyana bandha.
benefits: The benefits of Supta Konasana are the same as those for Baddha Konasana and Upavishta Konasana: the grdhrasi nadi becomes purified and the spinal column and waist become strong.

supta-padangushtasana.title: Supta Padangushtasana
notes: Supta Padangushtasana is a two-part asana: the first part has twenty vinyasas, the second has twenty-eight.
The 9th and 13th vinyasas are the states of the first part; the 11th and 19th vinyasas are the states of the second part.
While in the states of this asana, aspirants must be mindful to practice the breathing methods with attention — Guruji repeats this because the asana is unlike previous ones.

sequence.action: Part 1. Lie down on the back, as in the preparations for Sarvangasana, doing rechaka and puraka.

Bring the straightened right leg up toward the head, straighten the left leg, strongly take hold of the big toe of the right leg with the right hand, press the left hand firmly on the left thigh, and lie flat, keeping the head on the floor.
Lift only the head a little, touch the nose to the straightened right knee, and do puraka and rechaka as much as possible.
Lower the head to the floor.
Lower the right leg to the floor and join the legs together.
Repeat the above (vinyasas 8–11) for the left leg.
Come into the position of Halasana, press the hands to the floor by the ears, and roll the whole body back over the head into the position of the 4th vinyasa. This is called Chakrasana.
Remaining vinyasas as in previous asanas. End of Part 1.
Part 2. Perform the first ten vinyasas of Part 1.
Bring the right leg out to the right and lower it to the floor, and do rechaka and puraka as much as possible.
Raise the right leg and return to the 8th vinyasa of Part 1.
Touch the nose to the knee.
Lower the head to the floor.
Repeat the above (vinyasas 11–14) for the left side.

benefits: Supta Padangushtasana purifies and strengthens the waist region, knees, food and anal channels, and the sperm passageway (virya nala).
It dissolves the bad fat on the sides of the body and the waist, making the waist slender and strong, and the body light.
quotes: Indeed, whatever the asana, one should practice first on the right side and then on the left side.
supta-padangushtasana.state_label: 9 and 13 in part 1; 11 and 19 in part 2
cautions: Supta Padangushtasana can be done by all and sundry, except pregnant women.

surya-namaskara-a.title: Surya Namaskara A
surya-namaskara-a.title_as_printed: METHOD FOR DOING THE FIRST SURYA NAMASKARA
notes: Often practiced while chanting mantras.

Drishti: nasagra (tip of the nose) for Samasthiti; broomadhya (between the eyebrows) for the 1st vinyasa; nasagra for the 2nd; and so on — odd-numbered vinyasas gaze between the eyebrows, even-numbered vinyasas gaze at the tip of the nose.
For the even-numbered vinyasas, rechaka is performed; for the odd-numbered vinyasas, puraka.

sequence.action: Join the legs together, heels and big toes touching, push the chest up, lower the head slightly, and stand straight, gazing at the tip of the nose; this is Samasthiti, standing up in a straight line.
Raise the arms straight up over the head, bring the hands together, lean the head back a little, and look at the fingertips.
Bring the hands down to the floor on either side of the feet, straighten the knees, and touch the knees with the nose.
Lift only the head.
Press the hands squarely onto the floor and, with only the strength of the hands, throw the legs back and hold the body straight on the hands and toes only (Chaturanga Dandasana).

Push the chest forward with the strength of the hands, lift the head up, bend the waist, straighten the arms without touching either the thighs or knees to the floor, and extend the feet, toes pointed and tops pressed to the floor (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana).
Lift the waist up, tilt the head under, press the heels to the floor, pull in the stomach completely, and hold position, gazing at the navel (Adho Mukha Svanasana).
Jump the feet in between the hands, press the legs together, and stand with the knees straightened and feet joined, as in the 3rd vinyasa.
Bring the hands down to the floor on either side of the feet and touch the knees with the nose, as in the 2nd vinyasa.
Raise the arms straight up over the head, bring the hands together, lean the head back a little, and look at the fingertips, as in the 1st vinyasa.
Stand up straight in Samasthiti.

surya-namaskara-b.title: Surya Namaskara B
surya-namaskara-b.title_as_printed: METHOD FOR DOING THE SECOND SURYA NAMASKARA
notes: The rechaka and puraka of the second Surya Namaskara are the same as for the first; the 1st, 7th, 11th, and 17th vinyasas introduce a different form, and the remaining vinyasas are the same as those of the first.
For the even-numbered vinyasas, rechaka is performed; for the odd-numbered vinyasas, puraka.

sequence.action: Stand straight, joining the legs together, as in the first Surya Namaskara.

Bend the knees, which are together, lift the chest, raise the arms straight up over the head, join the hands together, lean the head back a little, and stand gazing at the tips of the fingers (Utkatasana).
Straighten the legs (do not bend the knees), press the hands down onto the floor on either side of the feet, as in the first Surya Namaskara, and touch the knees with the nose.
Straighten the back and lift the head only.
Jump the body back into the form of a stick with only the strength of the hands, as in the first Surya Namaskara, and rest with the head lifted a little.
Push the body forward with the force of the arms, lift the chest, arch the back, and make the legs tight and straight, resting with the tops of the feet pressed to the floor (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana).
Lift the waist up, press the heels to the floor, tilt the head, draw in the stomach tightly, and stare at the navel (Adho Mukha Svanasana).

Place the right foot between the hands, which are pressed to the floor, bend the knee of the right leg, straighten the thigh and knee of the left leg which is stretched back, raise the arms straight up over the head, bring the hands together, swell the chest, lean the head back a little, and rest, staring at the tips of the fingers.
Jump the body back into the form of a stick, as in the 4th vinyasa (Chaturanga Dandasana).
Push the body forward and lift the chest, as in the 5th vinyasa (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana).
Lift the waist, press the heels to the floor, and stare at the navel, as in the 6th vinyasa (Adho Mukha Svanasana).

As in the 7th vinyasa, but with the left leg forward: place the left foot between the hands, bend the knee of the left leg, straighten the right leg stretched back, raise the arms overhead, hands together, and rest, staring at the tips of the fingers.
Jump the body back into the form of a stick, as in the 4th vinyasa (Chaturanga Dandasana).
Push the body forward and lift the chest, as in the 5th vinyasa (Urdhva Mukha Svanasana).
Lift the waist, press the heels to the floor, and stare at the navel, as in the 6th vinyasa (Adho Mukha Svanasana).
Straighten the back and lift the head only, as in the 3rd vinyasa.
Straighten the legs, press the hands to the floor, and touch the knees with the nose, as in the 2nd vinyasa.
Bend the knees, lift the chest, raise the arms overhead, hands together, and stand gazing at the tips of the fingers, as in the 1st vinyasa (Utkatasana).
Then comes Samasthiti.
